title: Attested Vault Operator — Terraform proposal and runbook sketch
body:
Purpose:
This is a working proposal for an "attested vault operator" for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). The operator bundles: a Terraform module set to provision and maintain an integrated vault-like secrets service, an HSM/KMS adapter for customer FIPS/HSM-backed keys, and an audit forwarding pipeline that meets our audit retention requirements. This doc mixes architecture notes, Terraform module surface ideas, an upgrade/migration plan for existing customers, and an initial test/runbook checklist.

Goals (non-exhaustive):
- Provide a Terraform-first operator that can be deployed into customer VPCs or air-gapped environments.
- Ensure the operator can attest node identity and only provision keys into HSM-backed keyslots after attestation (TPM/SGX-like attestation or cloud instance identity).
- Minimize secrets exposure during bootstrap and upgrades; default to envelope encryption with HSM KEK wrapping.
- Offer an audit-forwarder that signs and ships immutable audit records to customer-managed log sinks and to Redwood control-plane for optional telemetry.
- Provide clear upgrade path from the legacy "secrets-guardian" module family with minimal downtime.

Design principles:
- Minimal runtime privileges: operator runs with least privilege; Terraform modules manage IAM/KMS/HSM resources but do not embed long-lived secrets.
- Default to KMS + HSM hybrid: use cloud KMS for lifecycle and HSM for root KEK where available.
- Attestation-first provisioning: require node attestation before unsealing or key provisioning steps.
- Observable by default: audit events must be emitted at every key lifecycle event (create/rotate/destroy/rollback).

High-level components (TF modules & runtime):
1) module/attested-vault-operator (root) — orchestration module
   - Variables: cluster_id, region, operator_image, attestation_mode (tpm|instance_identity|none), audit_sink_config, state_backend
   - Outputs: operator_endpoint, vault_ca_thumbprint, attestation_policy_id
   - Responsibilities: create operator deployment (k8s or systemd), bootstrap service account, wire other modules together.

2) module/kms-hsm-adapter — key management glue
   - Supports: cloud KMS (GCP/KMS, AWS/KMS), HSM appliance (PKCS#11 interface), HSM-as-a-service proxies (vendor-specific)
   - Variables: kek_key_reference, hsm_connection_uri, pkcs11_slot, kms_key_id
   - Behavior: configure key wrapping policy, ensure KEK is never exported in plaintext, create KMS grants for operator identity.

3) module/attestation-provider — attestation & identity
   - Supports: node TPM attestation flow, cloud instance identity tokens (GCP/STS/AWS instance identity), and YubiHSM serial-based attestation for air-gapped.
   - Outputs: short-lived attestation token, attestation_audit_proof
   - Notes: module may reference customer-specific CA for on-prem attestation; provide shim to handshake with Redwood attestation service if requested.

4) module/audit-forwarder — audit pipeline
   - Variables: sink_type (s3|gcs|syslog|splunk|elastic), signer_key_ref, retention_days
   - Responsibilities: sign every audit blob with operator signing key (rotated monthly), optionally mirror signed records to Redwood audit collector over mTLS.

State & locking considerations:
- Use remote state per-customer with locking (DynamoDB/Cloud SQL/consul for on-prem).
- Terraform plan/apply should be run by the operator controller in secured CI or customer-run runner; ensure the module supports an "operator-managed" mode and a "customer-managed" mode.

Upgrade / Migration plan (from existing 'secrets-guardian' stack):
Phase 0 — discovery (0–2 weeks):
- Inventory existing TF states (list KMS keys, secrets backends, credential grants).
- Collect runtime topology: number of VAULT replicas, sequence lengths cache, node attestation capability.

Phase 1 — parallel deployment (2–6 weeks):
- Deploy attested-vault-operator in parallel (new namespace/cluster).
- Configure KMS-HSM adapter but do not migrate KEKs initially; keep KEKs in legacy location and configure operator to read wrapped tokens.

Phase 2 — controlled key backfill (6–10 weeks):
- For each KEK, perform a wrap/unwrap test via HSM adapter and verify audit entry creation.
- Rotate application envelope keys to be wrapped by HSM KEK (one app at a time).

Phase 3 — cutover & decommission (10–12 weeks):
- Switch service discovery to point apps at operator endpoint, run warm-up and monitor error rates for 48–72 hours.
- If stable, remove legacy secrets-guardian infra (preserve snapshots).

Rollback plan:
- Keep last-known-good TF state and snapshot of secrets in encrypted archive (WORM if required).
- Re-enable legacy secrets-guardian ingress and restore previous KEK grants if rollback needed.

Security hardening specifics:
- HSM integration: require PKCS#11 interface and enforce FIPS 140-2 level (customer claim). Never allow raw unwrapped KEKs to be exported by operator runtime.
- Offline key ceremony: provide a documented key import/export process using signed blobs and multi-signer verification to admit KEKs into HSM slots.
- Envelope encryption: default server-side encryption for all state blobs, with server-side HSM KEK wrapping.
- Secrets-in-motion: all inter-component comms use mTLS with mutual client certs; operator will auto-rotate certs and publish thumbprints to audit sink.
- Audit integrity: every write (create/update/delete/key-rotate) emits a signed audit record containing previous/next key IDs, actor identity, attestation token fingerprint, and a monotonic sequence number.

Runbook snippets (operator failures):
- "Operator Crash Loop"
  1) Check operator logs (kubectl logs -n rvd attested-operator) for panic stack.
  2) Check attestation provider health endpoint. If attestation failing because of CA mismatch, re-issue attestation policy via module/attestation-provider.
  3) Fallback: scale down operator and promote legacy secrets-guardian by flipping toggle in feature_flags entity in config store.

- "HSM Unresponsive"
  1) Verify HSM network path (ping/proxy).
  2) Switch to read-only mode: operator continues serving existing wrapped secrets but refuses new key creation.
  3) Emit urgent alert to on-call and create high-priority incident.

Testing checklist (acceptance criteria):
- Attestation: operator only unseals when attestation token verified. Tests: simulate revoked CA, expired tokens.
- Key lifecycle: create/rotate/revoke path creates audit entries, wrapped by HSM KEK, and record verified signature.
- Disaster recovery: restore from encrypted snapshot into new cluster and verify audit chain continuity.
- Performance: benchmark envelope unwrap latency under expected QPS and validate tail latency < 75ms for key unwraps on target hardware.

Compliance mapping notes:
- SOC2: audit immutability and access logs, key rotation cadence documented.
- GDPR: ability for customers to redact or export audit records upon legal request; ensure retention policy configurable per-tenant.
- FedRAMP / DoD: support for HSM hardware-backed KEKs and offline key ceremony.

Operational concerns & open questions (unresolved):
- Which attestation backends are must-have for v0? TPM + cloud instance identity seems sufficient, but hardware TPM attestation for air-gapped needs more product discovery.
- Should Redwood offer a managed attestation CA as a convenience, or require customer-run CA for strict compliance? Pros/cons listed below.
- How do we handle multi-tenant key visibility when an operator instance supports multiple customers in a single cluster? Recommend per-tenant isolation via namespaces plus per-tenant HSM slots.
- Terraform workflow: do we require operator to run terraform apply (controller pattern) or provide IaC modules and recommend customer-managed pipeline? Both modes are useful; operator-managed increases support surface.

Next steps (short term):
- Sync with Infra/SRE on state backend recommendations (Consolidate options and pick a default for hosted vs air-gapped). Owner: Arjun. Due: 2024-12-20.
- Spike: implement minimal PKCS#11 shim in Go to validate connectivity with vendor HSMs. Owner: Connor. Due: 2024-12-30.
- Draft Terraform module skeleton with variables/outputs above and open PR for review. Owner: Maya. Due: 2025-01-10.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally a working sketch — expect TODO blocks, rough priorities, and assumptions. Please add comments inline in the GitHub PR (linked above) or leave notes in Confluence page PRIV-ATT-001 for larger architectural debates.
